User has selected the official Espressif ESP32-S31 Korvo factory_demo as the final performance/platform demo, implemented USING OPENVELA, not by flashing ESP-IDF. Preserve the separate digit-recognition demo. Prior field-registration demo is superseded. Shared workspace /home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela. Official pinned source is being downloaded (main/UI already present) into backups/factory-demo-port/upstream/examples/esp32-s31-korvo/examples/factory_demo, commit recorded in upstream-commit.json. Current E402 SMP native services + WiFi + BLE + MEDIA build is still running: DO NOT change maintained sources or build inputs, do not start full builds, do not access serial/USB/boards. Write only inside YOUR private directory under backups/factory-demo-port. Use actual openvela APIs, preserve upstream notices/licenses, no mocked hardware success or invented performance. Do not spawn other workers. Source modifications stay private; root integrates after review. Need concrete code/candidate and concise result, not just advice. Keep required original factory capabilities in scope. Read local relevant instructions. English source/comments/public docs. Existing root s31-reference AGENTS restriction against UI is overridden by explicit user scope. Current LVGL is 9.x, upstream UI is 9.2.2. Existing native application example: openvela-dev/frameworks/runtimes/services/xmsdemo/platform and lvgldemo; framework uikit/window LVGL APIs. Build compile_commands reference is backups/product-integration-execution/build-v1/build/compile_commands.json. No full firmware build; small targeted compile checks are allowed after candidate prepared.

YOUR DIRECTORY: /mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/factory-demo-port-e403/assets-port

Own coffee image resource port and LVGL image loading. Inspect upstream main/coffee_assets.c/.h, assets/coffee and generated UI use. Create private candidate native coffee_assets implementation and deterministic host asset packaging/conversion tools with licenses and manifest pinned to upstream. Goal reproduce visual appearance/transparency without ESP-IDF esp_mmap_assets/esp_lv_decoder/PPA. Investigate existing openvela LVGL libpng/JPEG decoders and filesystem drivers and choose exact real support. Prefer compressed original assets with bounded on-demand decode/cache; 16 MiB PSRAM and flash shared with system matter. Upstream raw C image arrays are huge and need not be compiled if image sources already use coffee_assets_get_src(). Retain exact enum/symbol mapping. Provide sizes, max decoded memory, LVGL Kconfig/CMake dependencies, clean no-global-conflict registration/deinit and failure handling. Storage packaging must be concrete: can use dedicated ROMFS/app resources or SD native file driver, but do not assume source-tree path works on target. Do not modify GUI/backend files owned by other workers. Write contracts.md early and result.md with candidate files and validation of all expected images.

I’ll inspect the coffee asset mapping and openvela’s LVGL loaders, then write a private candidate with packaging tools and validation results. I’ll leave maintained sources, build inputs, and board access untouched.

All 45 mapped PNGs are present: 944,695 bytes compressed, versus 5,985,980 bytes decoded as ARGB8888. openvela already has libpng support. I’m using the original PNGs to preserve alpha, with a target filesystem resource directory and no duplicate decoder or filesystem registration.

The reference build enables libpng but no LVGL filesystem driver. The candidate will require LVGL’s existing POSIX driver and use a 2 MiB shared image cache budget; init will check that budget without changing it. The largest decoded image is the 800×480 background at 1,536,000 bytes. I’ll document decoder workspace separately from decoded pixel memory.

The packaging tool now checks the pinned Git blobs, all 45 enum mappings, PNG chunk CRCs, pixel data, and alpha channels. The native loader is written with failure cleanup and per-image cache invalidation. Next I’ll compile it against the reference headers and compare every image with a real libpng decode.

The native loader compiles successfully with the reference RISC-V compiler and headers. I’m now testing the actual openvela LVGL filesystem, decoder, and cache code on the host to check pixel accuracy, corrupt-file rejection, and cleanup without creating a display or accessing hardware.

All 45 images passed the real LVGL/libpng host test and matched the independent PNG decode byte-for-byte, including alpha. Corrupt-package rejection, zero-cache mode, repeated initialization, and preservation of unrelated cache entries also passed. The reference profile has ROMFS enabled but SD disabled, so I’m adding a ROMFS resource artifact alongside the SD package.

Both packages are ready: a 1,054,720-byte SD archive and a 1,011,712-byte ROMFS image. I’m finishing the integration notes with the target mount paths, memory limits, license provenance, and validation evidence. The native loader and all 45 images have passed host validation; target rendering and performance remain untested.

Private candidate ready: [result.md](/mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/factory-demo-port-e403/assets-port/result.md) and [contracts.md](/mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/factory-demo-port-e403/assets-port/contracts.md).

- All 45 mappings preserved; real LVGL/libpng decoding matches original pixels and alpha exactly.
- Deterministic SD archive and 1,011,712-byte ROMFS supplied.
- Native RISC-V `-Werror` compile and lifecycle/cache/error tests pass.
- 2 MiB cache limit; largest decoded image is 1,536,000 bytes.

Maintained sources and boards untouched. Target rendering/performance remain untested.
